## Key takeaways

- While Pipedrive offers a streamlined, visual pipeline-first approach with strong mobile capabilities, Nutshell is a cost-effective, full-featured, and user-friendly alternative with advantages in unlimited contact storage, AI CRM tools, award-winning support and more.
- Zendesk Sell is a close second, as it’s the most like Nutshell with the exception of a few missing features. HubSpot is a strong choice for B2B professionals needing depth in marketing automation, while Salesforce caters to those requiring enterprise-level customization, but both come with higher costs and complexity.
- When evaluating CRMs, B2B professionals should map their essential workflows, budget for implementation and support, and leverage free trials and demos to test real-world fit, considering factors like UI comfort and data migration ease.

Why Pipedrive users are switching:

- ⭐ **4.2/5 rating on G2:** Solid but not exceptional; missing features cited in 7% of reviews
- 🛑 **7% low-star reviews on Trustpilot:** Billing disputes and slow support are cited frequently
- 📊 **<1% CRM market share:** Smaller platform means fewer integrations and longer support queues

Pipedrive CRM is a popular sales-focused CRM used by over 100,000 companies in more than 170 countries. It positions itself as a simple, well-rounded choice for businesses of any size and an instrumental tool for making salespeople’s lives easy. While it’s undoubtedly a good CRM, it isn’t a good fit for everyone, and many teams eventually find themselves looking for Pipedrive alternatives due to the platform’s limitations.

Pipedrive comes with several challenges and downsides, including a lack of marketing features, difficulty with integrations, deal caps and poor customer support. It’s crucial to compare Pipedrive’s features, reviews, and costs with the best Pipedrive alternatives to find the CRM that provides the best value for your team.

To help you find the right CRM for your needs, we’ve compiled the **best Pipedrive alternatives in 2026**. Using this comparison guide can help you identify the alternatives and ensure you’re really [choosing a CRM](https://www.nutshell.com/blog/how-to-choose-a-crm) that _works for you_.

In this guide, we’ll start with a breakdown of Pipedrive’s CRM. Then, we’ll outline the criteria we used to evaluate these tools, compare the top alternatives at a glance, and dive into each option. Let’s get started!

## Pipedrive alternatives at a quick glance

Looking for a fast overview? Here’s how our eight alternatives rank and what they’re best suited for:

1. **[Nutshell](https://www.nutshell.com/blog/pipedrive-alternatives-crms-for-high-powered-sales-teams#nutshell)(5.0/5):** Best for B2B teams needing all-in-one sales, marketing and engagement
2. **[Zendesk Sell](https://www.nutshell.com/blog/pipedrive-alternatives-crms-for-high-powered-sales-teams#zendesk-sell) (4.6/5):** Best for sales-only teams, especially those using Zendesk Support
3. **[HubSpot](https://www.nutshell.com/blog/pipedrive-alternatives-crms-for-high-powered-sales-teams#hubspot) (4.5/5):** Best for marketing-heavy teams wanting deep sales and marketing integration
4. **[Salesforce](https://www.nutshell.com/blog/pipedrive-alternatives-crms-for-high-powered-sales-teams#salesforce) (4.2/5):** Best for enterprise-scale customization and complex sales processes
5. **[Zoho CRM](https://www.nutshell.com/blog/pipedrive-alternatives-crms-for-high-powered-sales-teams#zoho)(4.0/5):** Best for budget-conscious teams needing extensive customization
6. **[Freshsales](https://www.nutshell.com/blog/pipedrive-alternatives-crms-for-high-powered-sales-teams#freshsales) (4.0/5):** Best for teams wanting AI-powered lead scoring without complexity
7. **[Monday CRM](https://www.nutshell.com/blog/pipedrive-alternatives-crms-for-high-powered-sales-teams#monday-crm) (3.9/5):** Best for visual, customizable pipelines with project management
8. **[Copper](https://www.nutshell.com/blog/pipedrive-alternatives-crms-for-high-powered-sales-teams#copper)(3.5/5):** Best for Google Workspace users living in Gmail and Google Drive

## Understanding Pipedrive CRM

Before we dive into the best Pipedrive alternatives, let’s review some essential information about the Pipedrive CRM.

### Pipedrive pros

Pipedrive is a popular CRM for a reason. Here are some of the pros of using Pipedrive:

- **Ease of use:** Users and prospective buyers appreciate Pipedrive’s clutter-free user interface. Pipedrive strives to provide a simple and intuitive experience so that its users can focus on selling.
- **Sales management features:** Pipedrive also excels in its pipeline and sales management features. Customers on every plan can see an overview of their leads and communications, and customize their pipelines.
- **Useful extra features:** Under the hood, advanced features like email sync, templated email automation, and the ability to connect with one-click call integrations can propel any sales team toward its goals.

### Pipedrive cons

Despite its benefits, Pipedrive also has a few cons. Take a look at some of the disadvantages we see most often with Pipedrive:

- **Open deals limits:** One of the major downsides of Pipedrive’s CRM is the limit on the number of open deals you can have in your pipeline per plan. For example, if you’re on the Essential plan, you can’t have [more than 3,000 open deals](https://www.pipedrive.com/en/pricing) in your pipeline — or else you have to start paying nearly double for the next highest plan. What this means is that when your business grows and starts working more leads through its pipeline, Pipedrive forces you to pay more.
- **Lack of comprehensive CRM features:** Pipedrive is primarily built for sales teams, leaving marketing and support teams without much value. Furthermore, even the expensive plans often don’t report on what users actually want. Pipedrive’s reporting lacks capabilities like viewing how many touches a prospect got, setting custom date ranges, and reporting on activities across users.
- **Poor customer service:** Pipedrive’s customer support — or lack thereof — is one of the [most common complaints from their customers](https://www.g2.com/products/pipedrive/reviews/pipedrive-review-9159868). Countless users [express frustration with their phone support](https://www.g2.com/products/pipedrive/reviews/pipedrive-review-7627680), citing long wait times and responses that don’t actually address the users’ concerns.
- **Insufficient customization options:** Many businesses struggle with Pipedrive’s limited customizability. Many have voiced that automation and workflow depth feel limited or unintuitive, and that contact management and analytics constraints are a problem. Another common complaint is the lack of native integrations and complex API requirements for custom connections.

![Bar chart showing the most common complaints about Pipedrive CRM based on G2 user reviews, with missing features cited most frequently](https://www.nutshell.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/Common-Pipedrive-Complaints-on-G2-1024x640.webp)

### Pipedrive pricing

Pipedrive’s price starts at [$19 per user per month](https://www.pipedrive.com/en/pricing), which is an attractive number when compared to many other CRMs.

But there’s a catch—that entry-level price point lacks many of its marquee features. This “Lite” version [leaves much to be desired](https://www.nutshell.com/nutshell-vs-pipedrive). Choosing this entry-level plan leaves you and your team without the ability to sync your email account to Pipedrive, no email or task automation, and no user/admin permissions.

Its Growth plan is the next tier up, starting at $34 per user per month, which opens access to a few core features with restrictions. You’ll be able to sync one email address per user with Pipedrive, but you still won’t be able to create a team or adjust user/admin permissions.

Bumping up to the $64 per user per month Premium plan will give you access to more features, but you’ll still be subject to deal, team, sequence, permissions, automation, and email sync limitations.

Lastly, Pipedrive offers the “Ultimate” plan, which costs $89 per user per month and offers higher limits and phone support.

## How we selected the best Pipedrive CRM alternatives

When evaluating Pipedrive competitors, we considered the following key criteria:

- **Feature set:** Robust sales pipeline management is a must, along with contact management, automation, reporting, AI tools, and (ideally) marketing and engagement features.
- **Pricing & value:** Affordable entry-level plans and scalable pricing as your team grows. We noted if a tool has free plans or if costs escalate with add-ons.
- **Ease of use:** An intuitive interface and low learning curve for quick adoption. A CRM only delivers value if your team actually uses it.
- **Integrations and ecosystem:** Ability to connect with email, marketing, support, and other tools (either natively or via integrations) to fit into your workflow.
- **Customer support:** Access to helpful support resources or live help when you need it. Great support can make onboarding and troubleshooting much smoother.

Using these criteria, we identified the most relevant and widely used CRM alternatives to Pipedrive for 2026. Below is a quick comparison table, followed by in-depth reviews of each tool.

### What we validated

Our analysis included:

- **Real user feedback** from 2,500+ verified reviews on G2 and Capterra
- **Feature parity testing** with realistic sales scenarios (pipeline management, email logging, reporting)
- **Pricing accuracy** verified directly from vendor websites (January 2026)
- **Support responsiveness** tested through live chat and email
- **Migration complexity** based on documented case studies and vendor migration tools

Using these criteria, we identified the most relevant and widely used CRM alternatives to Pipedrive for 2025. The result? Eight solutions that address the specific pain points driving Pipedrive users to switch.

## Why companies are leaving Pipedrive in 2026

Pipedrive’s limitations aren’t just complaints—they’re documented trends across industry reviews and migration case studies. Here’s what’s driving the shift away from Pipedrive.

### Feature gaps are the top complaint

On G2, “missing features” ranks as the #1 complaint about Pipedrive, cited in 7% of all reviews (179 mentions out of 2,569 reviews as of July 2025). The most common gaps include:

- Limited reporting customization (can’t set custom date ranges or view activity touchpoints)
- Thin marketing automation features (essentially non-existent)
- Rigid workflow automation (limited customization for complex sales processes)
- Restricted integrations (many require custom API work rather than native connections)

### Pricing complexity creates sticker shock

Pipedrive’s entry-level plan ($19/user/month) lacks essential features like email sync, automation, and user permissions. Teams inevitably upgrade to the Growth plan ($34/user/month) or Premium ($64/user/month)—a 180-300% price jump for core functionality that competitors include on base plans.

The result? A growing number of specialized migration services now focus exclusively on moving teams out of Pipedrive (Trujay, Import2, Instrumental Group)—a trend that signals widespread dissatisfaction.

### Support responsiveness is a common frustration

On Trustpilot, approximately 7% of reviewers (201 out of 2,871) assign one to two stars, often citing slow support response times and billing disputes. This support gap becomes critical during implementations and data migrations.

### The shift toward all-in-one platforms

In 2025, businesses are moving decisively away from single-purpose, vertical CRM systems toward flexible, integrated platforms that unite sales, marketing, and engagement. Pipedrive was built for sales teams only, leaving marketing and customer success teams without meaningful functionality.

Teams managing modern sales cycles—which require marketing nurturing, customer engagement, and post-sale support—increasingly see Pipedrive as too narrow.

## The 8 best Pipedrive alternatives for 2025

If you’re considering Pipedrive, it’s likely that you’ve heard of these alternatives or seen them on software review sites. While the bulk of their features are similar, each has its own unique pros and cons, which, depending on your needs, could make or break your CRM experience.

Check out these eight Pipedrive alternatives:

### 1\. Nutshell

**Rating:** 5.0/5

**Best for B2B teams needing an intuitive all-in-one CRM with built-in marketing and engagement.**

#### Summary

[Nutshell](https://www.nutshell.com/) is an award-winning [CRM platform](https://www.nutshell.com/blog/what-does-crm-do) and the best Pipedrive alternative. It helps B2B sales, marketing, and customer teams work together to close more deals and elevate customer experiences.

Powerful enough to support any element of your business and simple enough to implement without a paid admin or IT department, Nutshell is favored among small to medium-sized companies who know better than to overpay for software they’ll never use.

[According to customer reviews](https://www.g2.com/products/nutshell/reviews), Nutshell’s features often outshine its competitors in terms of both usability and comprehensiveness.

#### Key Features

- [**Enhanced contact management:**](https://www.nutshell.com/crm/contact-management) Store unlimited records, track timelines, and segment audiences with ease.
- [**Advanced pipeline automation:**](https://www.nutshell.com/crm/sales-automation) Drag-and-drop boards, multiple pipelines, and assignment rules streamline sales ops.
- [**Leading native marketing tools:**](https://www.nutshell.com/marketing) Build segments, send campaigns, and automate follow-ups without leaving the CRM.
- [**Robust reporting and forecasting:**](https://www.nutshell.com/reports) Ready-made and custom dashboards reveal pipeline health and revenue outlook.
- [**Top-notch integrations:**](https://www.nutshell.com/integrations-category/all) Over 5000 popular integrations (Google/Microsoft, QuickBooks, Zapier) keep work connected.
- [**AI-powered productivity:**](https://www.nutshell.com/ai) Leverage AI tools, like Nutshell’s AI chatbot, email reply starters, meeting/call summaries, voice-to-text, lead research assistant, and more.
- [**World-class customer engagement tools:**](https://www.nutshell.com/marketing) 1:1 and bulk SMS plus web chat keep conversations centralized inside Nutshell.
- [**Free onboarding data import assistance:**](https://support.nutshell.com/en/articles/8429032-import-nutshell-s-white-glove-support-services) Switching to Nutshell is easy with its white-glove import service ready to take care of your data importing needs.

#### Pros

- **User-friendly UI:** Clean, clutter-free design makes onboarding fast and keeps reps focused on selling.
- **Built-in email marketing:** Create [broadcasts and drip campaigns](https://www.nutshell.com/marketing/email-marketing) in the same place you manage deals.
- **Automation and AI:** [Pipeline rules](https://www.nutshell.com/crm/sales-automation), reminders, and [AI tools](https://www.nutshell.com/ai) (summaries, voice-to-text, research) cut busywork.
- **Affordable with no limits:** All plans include unlimited contacts/storage and live support—no surprise caps or add-ons.
- **Excellent support:** Real humans by phone and email help you solve problems quickly.
- **Easy migration and onboarding:** Import Pipedrive (and other CRM) data in a few clicks, with free white-glove assistance.

#### Cons

- **Fewer niche integrations:** The marketplace covers popular tools, but it isn’t as vast as Salesforce’s.
- **Lower name recognition:** A smaller brand presence, though customers often get more personalized attention.

#### Pricing

- **Sales Foundation:** $13/user/month
- **Sales Growth:** $25/user/month
- **Sales Pro:** $42/user/month
- **Sales Business:** $59/user/month
- **Sales Enterprise:** $79/user/month

_Note that Nutshell users on_ [_any Sales plan_](https://www.nutshell.com/crm) _can access and use features on its_ [_Marketing Foundation_](https://www.nutshell.com/marketing) _and_ [_Engagement Foundation_](https://www.nutshell.com/engagement) _plans._

#### Watch out for

### 2\. Zendesk Sell

**Rating:4.6/5**

**Best for sales teams wanting strong lead management and native communication, especially with Zendesk Support.**

Note: Zendesk announced on September 9, 2025 that it has decided to [retire Zendesk Sell](https://support.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/9591462550042-Announcing-the-retiring-of-Zendesk-Sell), with existing customers able to retain access to their Zendesk Sell data until August 31, 2027.

#### Summary

[Zendesk Sell](https://www.zendesk.com/sell/) is a sales-first CRM with streamlined lead tracking, deal management, and built-in calling/SMS, that keeps reps moving fast. It shines if you also use Zendesk for support, thanks to tight ecosystem alignment. Note that marketing automation isn’t native, so full-journey campaigns require additional tools.

#### Key Features

- Lead and contact management: Centralized database with tools to capture, qualify, and convert leads.
- Pipeline tracking: Customizable deal pipelines with drag-and-drop functionality similar to Pipedrive.
- Communication suite: Integrated calling, SMS, and email tools with activity tracking and templates.
- Task and activity management: Built-in reminders and task automation help reps follow up consistently.
- Mobile CRM: iOS and Android apps designed to keep sales teams connected in the field.

#### Pros

- **Simple, modern UI:** Highly rated for being easy to learn and navigate, keeping reps focused on selling rather than data entry.
- **Strong lead and pipeline management:** Capture, track, and qualify leads in a structured process with customizable deal pipelines.
- **Built-in communication tools:** Email integration, power dialer, and SMS functionality let reps manage outreach directly in the CRM.
- **Mobile-first design:** The mobile app is praised for being fast, reliable, and enabling reps to manage their pipeline on the go.
- **Zendesk ecosystem integration:** Works seamlessly with Zendesk Support, enabling a unified view of customer interactions across sales and service.

#### Cons

- **Limited marketing features:** Unlike Nutshell, Zendesk Sell lacks built-in email marketing or campaign management, requiring third-party tools for marketing automation.
- **Pricing can climb quickly:** Add-ons for advanced features and higher seat counts increase overall costs.
- **Less flexibility for complex reporting:** While reporting covers basics well, advanced analytics may be limited compared to Salesforce or HubSpot.

#### Key Features

- **Lead and contact management:** Centralized database with tools to capture, qualify, and convert leads.
- **Pipeline tracking:** Customizable deal pipelines with drag-and-drop functionality similar to Pipedrive.
- **Communication suite:** Integrated calling, SMS, and email tools with activity tracking and templates.
- **Task and activity management:** Built-in reminders and task automation help reps follow up consistently.
- **Mobile CRM:** iOS and Android apps designed to keep sales teams connected in the field.

#### Pricing

While [Zendesk Sell is no longer available to purchase](https://www.nutshell.com/blog/best-zendesk-sell-alternatives), this is what existing customers pay:

- **Team:** $19/user/month
- **Growth:** $55/user/month
- **Professional:** $115/user/month
- **Enterprise:** $169/user/month

#### Watch out for

While Zendesk Sell is a solid sales tool, you’ll need to consider a CRM alternative. As Zendesk has announced the [retirement of Sell](https://support.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/9591462550042-Announcing-the-retiring-of-Zendesk-Sell), existing customers may face long-term support and updates limitations. It may be helpful to note that Nutshell offers quick and easy migration from Zendesk Sell, with [free white-glove onboarding](https://support.nutshell.com/en/articles/8429032-import-nutshell-s-white-glove-support-services) to ensure the transition is seamless.

### 3\. HubSpot

**Rating: 4.5/5**

**Best for inbound teams that need a CRM tightly integrated with powerful marketing tools.**

#### Summary

Powerful builders and workflows let teams launch pages, forms, and multi-step campaigns without stitching tools together. ## How to migrate from Pipedrive to a new CRM

Switching CRMs may seem daunting, but the process is straightforward with the right plan in place. Here’s how to do it efficiently:

### Step 1: Export your Pipedrive data

Navigate to Settings → Data → Export in Pipedrive and download your contacts, companies, deals, and activities. Pipedrive allows CSV exports, which most modern CRMs can import.

**Tip:** Export separately by data type (contacts, companies, deals) to make mapping easier.

### Step 2: Clean and deduplicate your data

Before importing data into a new system, audit it thoroughly. Remove duplicates, standardize naming conventions, and fill in critical missing fields. This step prevents carrying over Pipedrive’s data quality issues into your new platform.

**Pro tip:** Use a data cleaning tool, such as Zapier, or a migration service to automate this step.

### Step 3: Map fields to your new CRM

Each CRM structures data differently. Create a mapping document that shows how Pipedrive fields align with your new CRM’s field structure. For example:

- Pipedrive “Custom Fields” → New CRM “Properties”
- Pipedrive “Pipeline Stages” → New CRM “Deal Stages”
- Pipedrive “Activities” → New CRM “Activity Timeline”

### Step 4: Test migration in a sandbox

Before going live, run a test migration in a sandbox environment to ensure everything is working as expected. Verify that the data was imported correctly, relationships between contacts and companies are intact, and deal history is preserved.

### Step 5: Train your team

Before full rollout, conduct training sessions covering:

- How to log activities and manage deals
- Where to find critical information (pipeline, reports, customer history)
- New workflows and automation rules
- How to use any new features your previous CRM lacked

### Step 6: Go live and monitor adoption

Execute the final migration during off-peak hours. Monitor for issues during the first week and provide rapid support to teams encountering challenges.

- **Timeline:** 2–3 weeks from start to full adoption
- **Cost:** Most migration services charge $1,000–$5,000, depending on data complexity. Nutshell’s Import2 partnership offers free white-glove migration, which can save significant time and expense.

## FAQs about Pipedrive alternatives

### 1\. Is there a free version of Pipedrive?

No—Pipedrive does not offer a permanent free plan. It only provides a 14-day free trial, after which paid plans start at $14 per user per month. If you’re looking for free options, HubSpot CRM and Zoho CRM both offer free tiers with limited functionality.

### 2\. What is the best free CRM alternative to Pipedrive?

HubSpot CRM is the most popular free alternative, with unlimited users and up to one million contacts. Zoho CRM also has a free plan for up to three users and includes pipeline tracking and workflow automation. These options are ideal for small teams who want to test a CRM before investing in a paid plan.

### 3\. What’s better, Pipedrive or HubSpot?

Pipedrive is great for teams that want a simple, sales-focused pipeline tool, while HubSpot shines for companies that need marketing and customer service integrations. Pipedrive is generally more affordable and easier to use out of the box, but HubSpot provides broader functionality if you’re willing to pay for higher-tier plans.

### 4\. How long does it take to migrate from Pipedrive to a new CRM?

Most migrations take one to two weeks from planning to go-live, depending on data volume and complexity. The process typically includes:

- **Days 1–2:** Export data from Pipedrive and audit for duplicates and quality issues
- **Days 3–4:** Map Pipedrive fields to your new CRM’s field structure
- **Days 5–7:** Execute test migration in a sandbox environment and verify data accuracy
- **Days 8–10:** Complete final migration to your live system
- **Days 11–14:** Train your team and monitor adoption

Many CRM vendors (including Nutshell, with its Import2 partnership) offer free white-glove migration assistance that handles the heavy lifting and reduces downtime.

### 5\. Does Nutshell have deal limits like Pipedrive?

No. Nutshell includes unlimited contacts, companies, and deals on every plan—including the entry-level $13/user/month plan. There’s no surprise tier upgrade when your pipeline grows. This is one of the biggest differentiators for teams leaving Pipedrive, where deal limits force painful mid-year plan upgrades.

### 6\. What should I look for when evaluating Pipedrive alternatives?

Focus on five key areas:

- **Feature set:** Does the CRM include sales pipeline, contact management, automation, reporting, and ideally marketing or engagement tools? Or will you need add-ons?
- **Pricing and value:** Compare total cost of ownership, not just per-user fees. Does the base plan include essential features, or do you need to upgrade for email integration or automation?
- **Ease of use:** Can your team get productive within hours, not weeks? Test the free trial with real workflows.
- **Integrations:** Will the new CRM connect natively with your email, calendar, and critical third-party tools? Or will you need workarounds?
- **Support quality:** Is live support included in your plan? What’s the response time? Do they offer migration assistance?

### 7\. Can I integrate Pipedrive with other tools?

Yes, Pipedrive integrates with email, calendar, and third-party apps, but with caveats. Integration complexity is a frequent complaint in reviews—many integrations require custom API setup rather than simple one-click connections. Better alternatives like Nutshell, HubSpot, and Salesforce offer more native integrations and cleaner marketplace ecosystems.

If your tech stack is heavy on integrations (marketing automation, customer support, accounting software), consider a platform with deeper integration support from day one.
